newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-DISPUTED GOAL GIVES U.S. WIN OVER NORWAY.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-DISPUTED GOAL GIVES U.S. WIN OVER NORWAY.

text.p: A disputed goal by Boston Bruin's Ted Donato with 46 seconds remaining in the first period aided the United States to a 3-1 win over Norway at the ice hockey world championships on Monday.
It moved the Americans, looking for the their first title in 64 years, level with Sweden atop the B pool standings with two wins apiece from their opening two games.
Russia, Slovakia and Italy also won their matches to keep alive their hopes of advancing to the medal round.
Norway, hammered 7-0 by Canada in their opening game on Saturday, bounced back against the Americans by taking an early 1-0 lead with a goal by Svien Enok Norstebo.

After Vancouver Canuck enforcer Don Brashear pulled the U.S. even it looked as if the teams would head into the first break tied until Donato stepped into the Norwegian goalmouth behind netminder Robert Schistad and stabbed home a loose puck.
Norway protested the goal but after checking with the video replay judges, referee Leonid Vaisfled allowed it to stand.

"The rule is if the puck is in the crease you can go after it," said Norway coach Brent McEwen. "But I really have to question whether you can go inside the net and take it from underneath the goalie.
"I have a real problem with that."
U.S. coach Jeff Jackson announced after the game that he will fill two of three spots still open on his roster with Chicago Blackhawks defenceman Erich Weinrich and netminder Chris Terreri.

He also said the thumb injury to defenceman Bryan Berard, sustained during Sunday's win over Latvia, was not as serious as first thought and the NHL rookie of the year candidate would remain with the team.
In Helsinki, once-powerful Russia struggled for much of their clash with Germany before a late three-goal burst secured them a 5-1 win.
Sergei Petrenko scored the all-important goal to put Russia 2-1 ahead midway through the second period, just 36 seconds after Bradley Bergen had brought Germany level at 1-1.
With the Germans once again pressing for an equaliser in the third period, defender Anatoly Fedotov hammered home a desperately needed insurance goal to give Russia a 3-1 lead.
Mikhail Sarmatin scored into an empty net and Alexei Morozov chipped in Russia's fifth two seconds from time to wrap up the scoring.
Slovakia who fought to a 2-2 draw against Russia on Sunday kept their hopes alive with a 5-3 win over France after recovering from two goals down.
The results left Russia and Slovakia with three points, one behind defending champions the Czech Republic who head Pool A with four points after two wins
In Pool B, Bruno Zarrillo scored twice as Italy stormed back from a three goal deficit to beat Latvia 5-4 for their first win of the championship.

Zarrillo, leading scorer in the German hockey league this season, tapped in a loose puck with just over 10 minutes remaining to cap the comeback and give the Italians victory after trailing 4-1 midway through the second period.
"They're a very talented team but we certainly didn't expect to be behind 4-1," said Italian coach Brian Lefley. "We had to stay patient and wait for our opportunities."
Latvia lost their opening match to the United States by the same score on Sunday.
